blurb: A derived capability, `capability Name = Kind`, can take options after the kind, each one positional literal that the compiler reads while it checks the program: `Service` takes `@worker("name")`, `R2` an optional `@jurisdiction("eu")`, `RateLimit` a `@limit(n)` and a `@period(d)`, and `Queue` a `@name("queue")`. The value must be a literal of the option's kind, and one the platform accepts: `@limit` a positive `Int`, `@period` `10.seconds` or `60.seconds`, `@jurisdiction` `"eu"` or `"fedramp"`, `@tls` (on a `MySql`) `"required"`, `"verify-ca"` or `"verify-identity"`, `@worker` a Worker name and `@name` a queue name, each of 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and `-` (a Worker name may also hold `_`). Each option is given once, and an `@worker` must name a Worker outside the project, since a context of your own is reached with `consumes`. A bad value would otherwise surface only when the platform refuses the deployment, so it is refused here. Use one of the values the note lists. `RateLimit` is experimental, so the project opts in under `[unstable]` in `bynk.toml`.
summary: A derived capability's option is not a single positional literal of its kind (string, positive `Int`, or an offered window), is given twice, or is a value the kind refuses (an `@worker` that is not a well-formed Worker name outside the project, a malformed queue `@name`, an unknown `@jurisdiction`).
